intro: School bus drivers handle a big vehicle, read children and keep strict schedules. The closest of the 25 careers below is Subway and Streetcar Operators, with an 89% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $86,380, which is 80% more than the $47,920 school bus drivers earn.
why_it_works: Every route means watching the road, the mirrors and dozens of children while keeping to a tight timetable. O*NET rates social perceptiveness at 3.25 out of 5 for this job and operations monitoring at 3.12. Transit, rail and passenger service jobs use the same skills. Almost every match needs no extra schooling. The skills to build are equipment maintenance and choosing equipment.
tips: Your commercial license and safety record are your strongest assets for transit and rail jobs.
Railroad Conductors and Yardmasters earn $78,000, which is 63% more, and railroads train new hires.
Transit agencies often hire school bus drivers for city routes with full-year schedules.

faq.q: What jobs can former school bus drivers do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Subway and Streetcar Operators (89%), Railroad Conductors and Yardmasters (78%) and railroad brake, signal and switch operators (76%), based on O*NET 31.0. Rail signal operators earn $68,840, which is 44% more than the $47,920 school bus median.

faq.q: Which careers for school bus drivers pay more?
faq.a: 16 of the 25 matches pay more. Commercial Pilots earn $123,220 (157% more), Transit and Railroad Police $90,230 (88% more) and subway and streetcar operators $86,380 (80% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Pilot and police roles need a certificate or academy first.

faq.q: Do school bus drivers need more education to switch?
faq.a: Rarely. 23 of the 25 matches need no more education than school bus drivers already have, including all of the top 10. In the closest match, 87% of workers have a high school diploma or the equivalent, and employers train on the job.

faq.q: What skills should school bus drivers learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are equipment selection, equipment maintenance, negotiation and managing materials. Coordination and service orientation already rate 3 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so mechanical knowledge is the main step toward rail and transit work.
